ForgeMCP Codex Blender Skills Integration

Date: October 29, 2026 Status: Repository skill and documentation integration; Blender runtime unchanged.

Source and author credit

The integration incorporates the 94-skill Blender Skills pack by Arjun Shukla (GitHub @arjun988 ↗, original repository ↗). The imported snapshot is commit 8f778d2405a214b508d4c7d80742be8e43acdd52 ↗. The upstream MIT license is preserved in LICENSES/blender-skills-MIT.txt, with attribution details in LICENSES/blender-skills-notice.md.

What changed

  • Added all 94 upstream specialist skills and their shared reference material under .agents/skills, the repository-local Codex skills directory.
  • Added the ForgeMCP forgemcp-blender skill and a current capability map for session discovery, scene inspection, supported typed recipes, creative previews, static-mesh transfer, render jobs, and evidence limits.
  • Adapted the upstream MCP execution and tool references to ForgeMCP. The instructions now route Blender work through ForgeMCP's native preview/apply tools and prohibit using an unrelated MCP adapter or arbitrary bpy execution.
  • Updated the ForgeMCP AGENTS.md, README, and encyclopedia indexes to route future Blender work through the bridge skill and record this integration.

The active Codex skill inventory lists the repository-local skill directory and the ForgeMCP bridge skill, confirming project skill discovery.

Acceptance and limits

Structural validation found 95 skill manifests total: all 94 upstream skills and one ForgeMCP skill. Names are unique and match their directories; all relative Markdown links resolve; the vendored MIT license is byte-identical to the upstream license. No Python host, Blender add-on, Unreal plugin, or MCP adapter code changed. This integration does not add Blender operations or claim support for every workflow in the production skills. Python tests and an Unreal target build were not relevant to this documentation-only change.

The ForgeMCP bridge preserves its existing evidence boundaries: scene apply does not save the active .blend; a render-job result does not establish visual approval; and a static-mesh export is not proof of Unreal import. Unsupported workflow phases remain explicit and require separate acceptance.
